newsitem.title: ITALY: Santer praises Italy for tough budget bill.
newsitem.headline: Santer praises Italy for tough budget bill.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer congratulated Italy on Friday for its plans to approve a deficit-cutting budget in an effort to join a single European currency.
"Contratulations to the Italian government..for this very courageous and very tough bill," Santer told reporters at a business conference in Venice.
"I know it is the will of the Italian government to be part of monetary union from the very first moment," Santer said.

The government was poised on Friday to approve the 1997 budget bill, which would be one of the most stringent in recent years, slashing a massive 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) off next year's public sector deficit.
The budget, far in excess of the 32.4 trillion lire package originally planned, aims to cut the ratio of deficit to gross domestic product (GDP) to three percent by the end of next year.
Achievement of the three percent deficit target would put Italy on course to join those countries establishing a single European currency in 1999.
"I don't know the exact details of the proposal on which an agreement (on the budget) has been reached, but I hope Italy can continue in this direction," Santer said.
